title: What Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Fault-tolerant quantum computers are quantum machines that correct their own errors faster than the errors accumulate. Physical qubits are fragile — noise flips them within microseconds — so fault tolerance encodes each logical qubit across many physical qubits and runs error-correction cycles continuously, allowing arbitrarily long quantum computations. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers in one line: Fault-tolerant quantum computers are quantum machines that correct their own errors faster than the errors accumulate.

Why it matters: Without fault tolerance, quantum computers stay limited to short demonstrations; with it, they can run the long algorithms (factoring, quantum chemistry, optimization) that motivate the field..
Where it is used: drug discovery and materials simulation, cryptanalysis, large-scale optimization, and quantum machine learning..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

title: Current Research State of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Research has demonstrated the core building blocks: repeated error-correction rounds that improve as the code distance grows, logical qubit operations, and suppression of logical error rates below physical error rates. Programs at major labs and startups are scaling from tens to thousands of physical qubits, targeting the first useful fault-tolerant logical qubits. The threshold theorem sets the bar: physical error rates must sit below roughly 1% for the leading codes. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.

description: The numbers that define Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers. Specifications are the contract between the idea and the build: hit them and the system works; miss them and it does not. Spec: Coherence time: 50 us - seconds depending on platform (must far exceed gate time)
Spec: Gate time: 10 ns - 100 us depending on platform
Spec: Syndrome measurement cycle: must run continuously, typically microseconds per round

t: Challenges and Open Problems in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
title: Challenges and Open Problems in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: The central challenge is overhead: thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit means millions of physical qubits for useful algorithms. Decoding syndromes in real time at microsecond rates strains classical control electronics. Crosstalk, leakage, and correlated errors break code assumptions, and every platform must improve physical fidelity while scaling manufacturing. Every challenge here is a design requirement in disguise: solve it and the technology moves forward. The pieces records each carry the challenge they exist to answer.

Challenge: Real-time decoding at microsecond syndrome rates
Challenge: Crosstalk, leakage, and correlated errors beyond code assumptions
Challenge: Scaling fabrication while improving physical fidelity
Challenge: Cryogenic and control I/O bottlenecks for millions of qubits
Challenge: Verifying that logical performance matches theory at scale
